Aiming, camera and on-screen feedback

This guide explains what the screen tells you while you move and aim, and the camera settings that change how movement feels.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 5 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Read the crosshair
  2. Steady ranged aim
  3. Read the looking-at card
  4. Status line and pickups
  5. Camera bob, speed view and damage dip
  6. Collection feed (survival)
  7. Water sounds and splashes
  8. Held items and the character portrait

Read the crosshair

The plus-shaped crosshair marks where your aim lands. By default it inverts the colours under it, so it stays readable over sky, grass and stone. In the rear third-person view it moves to the point you are aiming at. It is hidden in the front third-person view and while a menu is open. Crosshair and aiming reticle

  • With a bow, rifle or throwable in hand, the four lines spread apart as your accuracy drops. They close back into a plus as your aim steadies.
  • Other items keep the closed plus.
  • Raising the rifle's sights shows AIM above the crosshair. Holding Z to zoom shows ZOOM.
  • Settings > Interface > Crosshair sets CROSSHAIR STYLE (Cross, Dot or Brackets), CROSSHAIR SIZE (50 to 200 percent), CROSSHAIR COLOUR and CROSSHAIR OPACITY (25 to 100 percent). Adaptive colour inverts what is behind it; White, Lime and Cyan get a dark outline. Every style still opens with the spread.

Steady ranged aim

The spread of a bow, rifle or throwable depends on how you stand, move and shoot. Steadier aim for ranged weapons

Key or actionWhat it does
Hold Shift (crouch)Tightens the spread.
Moving on footWidens the spread. Faster movement widens it more.
In the airWidens the spread.
Bow drawA fuller draw steadies the aim.
Rifle sightsRaising the rifle's sights steadies the aim.
Rock wind-upA longer wind-up steadies a thrown rock. Dynamite and eggs have a fixed spread.
Each shotBriefly opens the reticle.
Hold Z (zoom)Narrows the view and slows mouse look. It does not steady the aim.

Read the looking-at card

When you aim at a block within 6 m, a card at the top right of the screen shows it. The card sits just left of the compact map. Looking-at card (F2)

  • The card shows the block's 3D icon, name and distance. The block icon stays still, so thin blocks such as doors stay readable.
  • The mining advice is one of: "CREATIVE INSTANT BREAK", the recommended tool, or "NO SPECIAL TOOL NEEDED".
  • An animal gets its own card, with its health. Its model turns slowly.
  • If furniture is between you and the block, the card is hidden. The hint under the crosshair names the furniture instead, for example "TABLE | BLOCKS TERRAIN INTERACTION". You cannot mine or build through it.
Key or actionWhat it does
F2Hide or show the card in the world.
Settings > Interface > Layout > TARGET INFO (F2)The same setting. It follows you between worlds.
Tip. The card is hidden while a menu is open.

Status line and pickups

Actions report in the status line at the top left. Status line, pickup and damage feedback

  • Mining a whole block reports "Collected <block> x<pieces>". Shift-mining one half-metre piece reports "Carved <block>". Pieces go straight into your pack.
  • A full pack says "Capacity full; block left behind". The block stays in the world, and "! Inventory full" shows in the lower right.
  • Opening your pack says "Inventory opened".
  • Mined blocks throw debris and play a break sound. Mining never leaves items on the ground; in survival, items you drop with J and animal drops lie there until you pick them up. Items on the ground and manual dropping
Good to know. A sudden loss of at least 1 HP, from a hit, a fall or a blast, plays a short hurt voice. Voices are at least half a second apart, and slow health drains stay silent. There is no red flash. In Survival, when a blast or an animal hurts you, a small arrow beside the crosshair points towards it for about a second. The camera dip is also a cue. See the camera section below.

Camera bob, speed view and damage dip

Three camera effects change how movement and hits feel. Each has a row in Settings > Gameplay > Movement. Camera bob and speed field of view

Key or actionWhat it does
CAMERA BOBWalking gently bobs the camera. Turn it off here.
SPEED FOVOff or On. On widens the view by up to 5 degrees at high horizontal speed, reaching full widening at about 16 m/s. Jumps and falls do not change it.
DAMAGE BOBOff, Reduced or Full. Full is the default. After a hit of at least 1 HP, the camera dips up to 7 cm at Full and half that at Reduced.
  • Speed FOV eases over about 0.3 s, so a sprint-jump does not pump the view.
  • Vehicles have their own speed effect, which the SPEED FOV row also turns off.
  • Only real health loss causes the dip. Hunger, respawn and loading do not.
  • The dip does not move what you aim at. Aiming and interaction still use your eye position.
Tip. The REDUCE MOTION accessibility setting also turns off the camera bob, Speed FOV and the damage dip.

Collection feed (survival)

In survival, a small feed in the lower-right corner lists what you gained, for example "+3 Oak wood". Lower-right collection feed

  • Gains come from mined blocks, felled trees, hunted animals, fishing catches, items you pick up from the ground, a chest you break, filled flasks, exploration finds and packed boats or homes.
  • A gain of an item that is already listed adds to its row.
  • Up to five rows show. Each stays for about 4 seconds and fades over its last 0.8 s.
  • Warnings such as "! Inventory full" sit above the gains for about 6 seconds. A repeated warning shows a count, for example "(x3)".
  • Creative mining, crafting, the creative catalog, home storage and loading a save show nothing.
  • The feed is hidden while a menu is open.

Water sounds and splashes

Water entry splashes and bubbles

  • Wading into water plays a small splash. A fall at hard-landing speed plays a big splash with more droplets.
  • After you leave the water, walk about 2 m on dry ground before the next splash plays.
  • Moving through water releases bubbles and a swim sound about every 1.4 m.
  • Rain makes small ripple splashes on surfaces.
  • A sailing boat moving faster than about 1.2 m/s throws small spray from its bow. Boats leave no wake.

Held items and the character portrait

Held items show only in first person. A block you select is shown as a full-size textured cube held out to the right; plants show as an upright cut-out and doors as a small upright door. Tools are held on the right, and the full-size bow sits just right of centre with its own string hand. With nothing in hand, or with a block you no longer carry in Survival, your bare right arm rests low on the right. Hold left click to swing a tool, bare hand or held block; bows and rifles do not swing. Placing a block plays one swing, and so does a throw. The swing is visual only. A held sailing boat shows no hand. F1 hides held items in the clean view. Held blocks and hands (first person)

Press E and open Pack; in Creative, E may open on Build first. Click the figure button beside the pack button; its hint says "Character". A 3D portrait of your explorer appears. Move the pointer across it to turn the model. It shows Creative or your health out of 100, and what you are holding. There are no appearance, outfit or skin options. Remote players in multiplayer use the same fixed explorer model. Character tab (portrait only)

How this guide was checked

Crosshair spread, aim steadiness, the looking-at card, the status line, camera effects, the collection feed and water effects come from the feature ledger, which cites Voxelgame source lines. The numbers were rechecked at Voxelgame commit 0494a0ce: 6 m target reach, Speed FOV 5 degrees reaching full at 16 m/s with a 0.3 s ease, a 7 cm damage dip on hits of at least 1 HP, 5 feed rows shown for 4 s with a 0.8 s fade, and 14 splash droplets. On 8 November 2026 the looking-at section was re-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c: voxelgame-render target_ui.rs:140-147 and 260-291, hud.rs:487-492, menus_ui.rs:181-195; voxelgame-core settings.rs:65, 82-89 and 598-616. On 8 November 2026 the status-line drop sentence, the camera settings route and the character portrait were re-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: game/item_drops.rs:102-137 and game/creature_melee.rs:71-81 (beneath crates/voxelgame-core/src/); voxelgame-core settings.rs:68-89; voxelgame-render inventory_ui.rs:461-480. Also on 8 November 2026, the crosshair, steady-aim, status, collection, water, held-item and portrait sections and the camera numbers were re-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: voxelgame-render reticle_ui.rs, hud.rs, hud/survival.rs, pickup_feed_ui.rs, viewmodel.rs, character_preview.rs, player_avatar.rs and inventory_ui.rs; voxelgame-core game/readouts.rs, settings.rs, game.rs, game/audio.rs, game/pickup_feed.rs, game/plant_support.rs, game/inventory_input.rs and game/inventory_qol/presentation.rs.
